Practice it long and longer still, and past faults can be dissolved and remaining calamity dispelled; as the later practice daily becomes complete, new blessing comes of itself. The foolish of today, knowing that what they have done is not good — perhaps their conscience has stirred — plan to rely on monks and Daoists to recite confession texts, hoping thereby to be released from guilt. This is truly to wish to save a cartload of firewood with a cup of water. Is it not a great delusion? Moreover, while former offenses are first repented, later faults are again added, until at last they sink forever in the sea of suffering, losing body and nature. How sad. If men repent and change in this way, do they not greatly betray the Most High's earnest admonition?

Alas, the Most High's method of teaching men to correct faults and the way of repentance are set out in a few words that are to the point, needling men to the blood. As it is said: one pellet of the divine elixir turns iron into gold; one word of perfect principle turns the ordinary into the holy. Men should pledge themselves and practice it with all their strength, so as to match his vast compassion. Now I will first make clear the method of repentance, and next the method of correcting faults. Repentance is the essential way of changing the past and cultivating the future, of producing good and extinguishing evil. Therefore the root of goodness should be tended, and all good will grow; the root of guilt should be exposed, and all guilt will be destroyed. First, right faith in cause and effect, neither deluded nor mistaken: doing good obtains blessing, doing evil incurs calamity; though there be no doer, the fruit of retribution is not lost; though thought after thought ceases, karma does not perish. Faith is the source of the Way, and wisdom is what can enter it. This is the root of all good; with this right faith one overturns and breaks the mind of the icchantika. Second, to repent of evil, taking shame as the foundation. I am ashamed of this guilt of mine, that it does not rank me among men; I am ashamed of this guilt of mine, that it must bring down Heaven's punishment. This is called the white dharma; it overturns and breaks the black dharma of shamelessness. Third, to fear impermanence: one breath does not return, and life is at once extinguished, and one receives retribution according to karma, revolving without end. Having awakened to impermanence, this overturns and breaks the mind that does not fear the evil paths. Fourth, to disclose: to tell others the weight of one's offenses. Because of the disclosure the guilt at once withers, as when the root of a tree is cut and its branches and leaves shrivel and fall. This is called overturning and breaking the mind of concealment. Fifth, to cut off the mind of continuation, to renounce evil decisively, resolved and courageous, as a keen blade cuts an object and severs it at a single stroke. This is overturning and breaking the mind of continuation. Sixth, to arouse the bodhi mind: to pull up all suffering universally and to give all joy universally. With this vast mind one overturns and breaks the mind that ranges over all evil karma everywhere. Seventh, to cultivate merit to make up for faults, diligently spurring the three karmas and advancing without rest. This is to cultivate merit and establish virtue, overturning and breaking the mind that does not cultivate the three karmas yet raises evil thoughts without cause. Eighth, to guard the true Dharma, not giving thought to outside paths and false teachers who destroy the Buddha Dharma. This is overturning and breaking the mind that extinguishes all good deeds. Ninth, to call on the buddhas of the ten directions, their measureless merit, their spiritual powers and wisdom, their compassionate protection, to rid me of guilt — the cool and wonderful medicine. This is overturning and breaking the mind that calls on evil friends. Tenth, to contemplate the emptiness of the nature of guilt: guilt arises from the mind and is extinguished again from the mind. Hence it is said: if the mind is extinguished, guilt too is gone. If one knows that guilt and blessing have no master and that the substance of the mind is empty of itself, then one returns to the root and goes back to the source and is at last pure. This is overturning and breaking the mind of ignorance, inversion, and clinging. The scriptures say: the sea of all karmic obstruction all arises from deluded thought; if one wishes to repent, sit upright and contemplate true reality; the mass of guilt is as frost and dew, and the sun of wisdom can dissolve it. Therefore one should repent with all one's heart. As a robe soiled for a hundred years can be washed in a single day and made fresh and clean, as an ancient mirror of a thousand years can be wiped in a moment and give forth light, so can one dissolve the faults of a thousand lives and ten thousand kalpas and extinguish the offenses of the four grave and five heinous acts. With such repentance, what evil will not be destroyed, what good will not be born?
